sentences.en: So today, to prepare us all for this upcoming spectacle, I talk with two people who've produced critically acclaimed and widely read interpretations of The Odyssey.

sentences.en: Emily Wilson, who translated The Odyssey and is the very first woman to do so, and Madeline
sentences.zh: 埃米莉·威尔逊，她翻译了《奥德赛》，并且是历史上第一位完成此壮举的女性，还有玛德琳

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你们好。

sentences.en: Happy to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴来到这里。

sentences.en: Yes, definitely.
sentences.zh: 对，绝对的。

sentences.en: This is going to be, like, the most exciting thing I do for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 这将会是我很长一段时间里做过的最让人兴奋的事情。

sentences.en: It is really making me love my job that we get to do this together.
sentences.zh: 一想到我们能一起完成这个，我就真的更加热爱我的工作了。

sentences.en: So, we have you both gathered here in order to talk about something that really fascinates me, has fascinated me for a long time, which is The Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们把两位聚在这里，是为了聊聊一个让我非常着迷、并且让我着迷了很久的主题，那就是《奥德赛》。

sentences.en: And we want to prepare people for this movie in a way that I think only the two of you can.
sentences.zh: 我们想以一种只有你们两位才能做到的方式，帮大家为这部电影做好准备。

sentences.en: But first, for people who may not remember the plot of The Odyssey, I am going to attempt a quick recap.
sentences.zh: 但首先，为了那些可能已经记不清《奥德赛》剧情的听众，我打算快速回顾一下。

sentences.en: The very, very short version is that it's the story of a man, Odysseus, who is trying to get home.
sentences.zh: 最简短的版本就是：这是一个名叫奥德修斯的男人试图回家的故事。

sentences.en: He fought in the Trojan War for 10 years, and then he spends 10 years working his way across the beautiful but also very scary Mediterranean Sea in order to get to the island
sentences.zh: 他参加了特洛伊战争，打了10年，然后他又花了10年时间，在美丽却也十分可怕的地中海艰难跋涉，最终要抵达

sentences.en: of Ithaca, which he is the king of and where his wife Penelope and son Telemachus are waiting for him.
sentences.zh: 伊萨卡岛，那是他的王国，他的妻子珀涅罗珀和儿子忒勒马科斯正在那里等着他。

sentences.en: It is all very dramatic because there are a bunch of suitors trying to get Penelope to betray Odysseus and marry one of them.
sentences.zh: 这一切都非常戏剧性，因为有一群求婚者正千方百计地想让珀涅罗珀背叛奥德修斯，并嫁给他们其中的一个。

sentences.en: And it is famously extremely difficult for him to actually get there, to get to Ithaca.
sentences.zh: 而且众所周知，他想要真正抵达目的地、回到伊萨卡是极其困难的。

sentences.en: There is sex and murder along the way.
sentences.zh: 这一路上伴随着色欲与谋杀。

sentences.en: There are fantastical creatures, vengeful gods, helpful gods, awesome gods.
sentences.zh: 有离奇的生物、复仇的神明、善良的神明、令人敬畏的神明。

sentences.en: The whole point of it is that he is really smart and really resourceful, and he gets home
sentences.zh: 整个故事的核心在于，他极其聪明且足智多谋，他最终能够回家

sentences.en: eventually not because he's the strongest dude in the world and really good at war, but because he essentially outsmarts his enemies.
sentences.zh: 并不是因为他是世界上力气最大的人、打仗最厉害，而是因为他本质上智胜了他的敌人。

sentences.en: Emily, I hope I did an okay job with that.
sentences.zh: 埃米莉，希望我刚才概括得还算可以。

sentences.en: That was great.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Transconscious, doing it in front of you.
sentences.zh: 当着你的面做这个，真是需要超常的意识。

sentences.en: What was it about that story that first got you, that hooked you?
sentences.zh: 是这个故事的什么特质最先吸引了你、迷住了你？

sentences.en: So going back to childhood, I mean, my first exposure to a version of that story was when, as for many people, was when I was a little kid and I got to be in a school play.
sentences.zh: 追溯到童年，我是说，我和这个故事的初次接触，和很多人一样，是在我还是个小女孩的时候，我有机会参演了一场学校话剧。

sentences.en: I got to play Athena.
sentences.zh: 我有幸扮演雅典娜。

sentences.en: I thought, this is such an exciting story about goddesses, and there were these kick-house goddesses.
sentences.zh: 当时我想，这是一个多么激动人心的关于女神的故事啊，而且这些女神个个都酷炫无比。

sentences.en: Who doesn't love stories with gods, with giants, with the possibility of being eaten alive?
sentences.zh: 谁能不爱那些有神明、有巨人的故事，还有随时可能被生吞活剥的刺激感呢？

sentences.en: That's exciting.
sentences.zh: 这太让人兴奋了。

sentences.en: And these questions about whether forces that are more powerful than you might be plotting and you're in the midst of these mysterious plots and you don't know where you are in
sentences.zh: 还有这些关于“比你更强大的力量是否正在暗中谋划”的疑问，而你正身处于这些神秘的阴谋之中，却不知道自己身在世界的何方。

sentences.en: the world.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说，与童年的体验有着极强的共鸣。

sentences.en: That, to me, very much resonates with the experience of childhood.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说，与童年的体验有着极强的共鸣。

sentences.en: And then once I was older, I got to learn Greek, and Homer in Greek sounds fantastic.
sentences.zh: 后来我长大了，开始学习希腊语，而希腊语原汁原味的荷马史诗听起来棒极了。

sentences.en: And that also hooked me in a whole new way to how it sounds on the level of the line, the passage, the voice, the speech, and the rhythms of the language.
sentences.zh: 这也以一种全新且深入的方式吸引了我——被它在诗行、段落、声音、言辞以及语言韵律层面的美感所折服。

sentences.en: And also, I was hooked on just how fascinatingly complex the storytelling techniques of this ostensibly very simple story are, and how psychologically deep and subtle it is.
sentences.zh: 同时，我也被这个表面上看极其简单的故事背后，那迷人且极其复杂的叙事技巧，以及它深邃且细腻的心理描写深深吸引。

sentences.en: It's not just a kid's adventure story.
sentences.zh: 它不仅仅是一个给小孩子看的冒险故事。

sentences.en: It also has so much to say about these really deep questions about grief and rage and loss and whether full recovery or going back in time is ever possible.
sentences.zh: 它还蕴含着对悲伤、愤怒、失去等深层问题的深刻探讨，以及探讨了是否真的存在完全的救赎或时光倒流的可能。

sentences.en: What about you, Madeline?
sentences.zh: 你呢，玛德琳？

sentences.en: What is your Odyssey origin story?
sentences.zh: 你的“奥德赛”起源故事是什么？

sentences.en: How did you get sucked into this weird, amazing world?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么陷入这个奇妙而诡异的世界的？

sentences.en: Well, my mother, who was an English major and a librarian and also loved mythology, started
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的母亲曾主修英语专业，当过图书管理员，并且也非常热爱神话，当我年纪还很小的时候，她就开始

sentences.en: reading me little pieces of the Iliad and the Odyssey as bedtime stories when I was pretty young.
sentences.zh: 把《伊利亚特》和《奥德赛》的片段当作睡前故事读给我听。

sentences.en: And I fell in love with it.
sentences.zh: 我一下子就爱上了它。

sentences.en: I wanted more and more.
sentences.zh: 我渴望听到更多。

sentences.en: In particular, the thing that really grabbed me was actually Penelope's trick.
sentences.zh: 特别是，真正抓住我的其实是珀涅罗珀的计谋。

sentences.en: That was one of the pieces of the story that, as a kid, I remember loving because her trick is that the suitors are trying to kind of force her to choose one of them to marry.
sentences.zh: 那是故事中我作为一个孩子时就记得并深深喜爱的情节之一，因为她的计谋是：求婚者们强行逼迫她在他们当中选择一个人结婚。

sentences.en: She's waiting for Odysseus to come home.
sentences.zh: 而她在等待奥德修斯回家。

sentences.en: And so she tells them, OK, I'll choose after I finish weaving this shroud.
sentences.zh: 于是她告诉他们：“好吧，等我织完这件寿衣，我就做决定。”

sentences.en: And then, you know, she weaves it.
sentences.zh: 然后，你知道的，她白天织布。

sentences.en: And then at night she goes and unravels it.
sentences.zh: 到了晚上，她就去把织好的拆掉。

sentences.en: And then she weaves it and unravels it.
sentences.zh: 白天织，晚上拆。

sentences.en: And it's such a great trick on so many levels.
sentences.zh: 从很多层面上来看，这都是一个绝妙的计谋。

sentences.en: It's so smart.
sentences.zh: 它太聪明了。

sentences.en: But also she knows that they have no idea how long it takes to weave a shroud.
sentences.zh: 而且她深知这些男人根本不知道织一件寿衣到底要花多长时间。

sentences.en: And so it's like a great trick that like really reveals sort of the gender roles of the time as well.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个绝妙的计谋，它也很真实地揭示了那个时代的性别角色。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: These men have absolutely no idea what shroud making entails.
sentences.zh: 这些男人根本不知道制作寿衣需要经历什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I love that not only is this about a very clever and ingenious man, it's also about a very clever and ingenious woman who's his his match in every way.
sentences.zh: 所以我很喜欢这一点：这个故事不仅关乎一个极其聪明机智的男人，也关乎一个极其聪明机智的女人，她在各方面都与他不相上下。

sentences.en: OK, Emily, I want to ask about the project of translating the Odyssey, because obviously we credit Homer with this story, but we know that this is something that was told over many
sentences.zh: 好的，埃米莉，我想问一下关于翻译《奥德赛》这个项目的问题，因为显然我们将这个故事归功于荷马，但我们也知道这是经过许多

sentences.en: generations.
sentences.zh: 代人流传下来的东西。

sentences.en: It was an oral tradition refined and shaped by different tellers, these bards.
sentences.zh: 这是一个口头传统，由不同的讲述者——也就是这些吟游诗人——不断打磨和塑造。

sentences.en: Homer kind of did the original interpretation in a way.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，荷马完成了最初的诠释。

sentences.en: And since then, in the modern era, there have been many translations into English.
sentences.zh: 自那以后，在现代，已经有了许多英语译本。

sentences.en: So why did you decide to translate it again?
sentences.zh: 那么，你为什么决定再次翻译它呢？

sentences.en: And what was the opportunity that you saw here to do something that hadn't been done before?
sentences.zh: 你在这里看到了什么机遇，能去做一些前人未曾做过的事情？

sentences.en: I felt so grateful to get to spend, you know, these many, many years working on the Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 能够花这么、这么多年时间来从事《奥德赛》的翻译工作，我感到非常感激。

sentences.en: It was just so fun.
sentences.zh: 这实在是太有趣了。

sentences.en: The opportunity I saw was partly about trying to activate elements of the original in contemporary English that I felt were not fully activated in the many translations that
sentences.zh: 我看到的机遇部分在于，试图在当代英语中激活原作中的那些元素——在我看来，在我曾尝试与学生们一起使用的众多译本中，这些元素并未被充分激活。

sentences.en: I'd tried using with my students.
sentences.zh: 在我曾尝试与学生们一起使用的众多译本中，这些元素并未被充分激活。

sentences.en: And one of the big elements that I felt wasn't fully activated was the meter.
sentences.zh: 而我深感未被充分激活的核心要素之一就是格律。

sentences.en: The fact that the original isn't just a story, it's a poem.
sentences.zh: 原作不单单是一个故事，它是一首诗。

sentences.en: It has rhythm.
sentences.zh: 它有韵律。

sentences.en: It's designed for oral performance.
sentences.zh: 它是为口头表演而设计的。

sentences.en: And so it seemed to me that I needed to use traditional poetic form, the meter of Shakespeare
sentences.zh: 因此在我看来，我需要使用传统的诗歌形式——莎士比亚和弥尔顿所用的格律

sentences.en: and Milton, in order to activate for an English listener or English reader some elements of what did Homer sound like to a fluent listener of the original.
sentences.zh: ——来为英语听众或英语读者唤醒一些特质：对于精通原作语言的听众来说，荷马听上去究竟是什么样的。

sentences.en: Just to be clear, when you're talking about the meter, what you did with this is write it in iambic pentameter.
sentences.zh: 为了说清楚，当你在谈论格律时，你在这部译本中采用的是五音步抑扬格。

sentences.en: And it sounds like you're saying that that rhythm, that pace was crucial to the original text and you didn't read it represented in these other translations.
sentences.zh: 听上去你的意思是，那种韵律和节奏对原作文本至关重要，而你在其他译本中没有读到这种还原。

sentences.en: And I just, it's so bananas that you did that.
sentences.zh: 而我只是觉得，你竟然做了这件事，简直太疯狂了。

sentences.en: It sounds so hard.
sentences.zh: 听上去就难得不可思议。

sentences.en: You also kept it the same number of lines as the original Homer.
sentences.zh: 你还保持了和荷马原作完全相同的行数。

sentences.en: It just sounds very, very difficult.
sentences.zh: 这听起来真的、真的很困难。

sentences.en: Like, extremely hard.
sentences.zh: 简直难到极点。

sentences.en: Did it take you as long as Odysseus to get that?
sentences.zh: 你花的时间是不是和奥德修斯回家一样久？

sentences.en: I could easily have used 20 years.
sentences.zh: 我完全可以花上20年。

sentences.en: If the publisher said, let me have 20 years, I would have used every second of it.
sentences.zh: 如果出版商对我说“给你20年吧”，我会把每一秒钟都用尽。

sentences.en: Yes, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对会。

sentences.en: So, the original is composed in the meter that was common, traditional for epic verse in archaic
sentences.zh: 那么，原作所采用的格律是古希腊史诗中常见且传统的格律

sentences.en: Greece, which is dactylic hexameter.
sentences.zh: ，也就是达梯体六音步（dactylic hexameter）。

sentences.en: Doesn't exactly roll off the tongue, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，这名字读起来可真不太顺口。

sentences.en: Andra, my enepe, musa, polythropon, hosma la pola.
sentences.zh: （希腊语朗诵示范）

sentences.en: And it has that rhythm all the way through.
sentences.zh: 它从头到尾都保持着这种韵律。

sentences.en: So it has this traditional meter.
sentences.zh: 所以它拥有这种传统的格律。

sentences.en: I'm not the first translator to use iambic pentameter in English, but I'm very rare in doing that in the modern era.
sentences.zh: 我并不是第一个在英语中使用五音步抑扬格的译者，但在现代，这样做的人极其罕见。

sentences.en: It's something that earlier translators, early modern translators assumed that, of course, meter needs to be translated into meter.
sentences.zh: 这是早期译者——早期现代译者所理所当然的事情，他们认为格律自然应该被翻译成格律。

sentences.en: Whereas in the modern era, there's been this assumption that modern readers can't tolerate rhythm, which I think is false.
sentences.zh: 然而在现代，人们有一种假设，认为现代读者无法忍受韵律，我认为这是不对的。

sentences.en: I think modern readers can totally tolerate rhythm and, in fact, love it.
sentences.zh: 我认为现代读者完全能够忍受韵律，事实上，他们非常热爱韵律。

sentences.en: Can you just read a little from your translation to give us a sense of that?
sentences.zh: 你能否从你的译作中朗读一小段，让我们感受一下这种韵律？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: So I can read from the episode in which Odysseus and his men have to pass through the strait
sentences.zh: 我可以读一段这样的情节：奥德修斯和他的船员们必须穿过海峡

sentences.en: between two terrible goddesses, one of whom is a whirlpool who threatens to swallow their whole ship.
sentences.zh: ，经过两个可怕的女神，其中一个是会威胁要吞噬他们整艘船的漩涡。

sentences.en: And the other is a six-dog-headed deity who will eat up six of the men from every ship that passes by, depending on which side the ship veers towards.
sentences.zh: 而另一个则是拥有六个狗头的神明，无论船只偏向哪一边，它都会从每一艘经过的船上吃掉六名船员。

sentences.en: So we rode through the narrow strait in tears.
sentences.zh: 于是我们含泪驶过了狭窄的海峡。

sentences.en: On one side, Scylla.
sentences.zh: 一边是斯库拉。

sentences.en: On the other, shining Charybdis with a dreadful, gurgling noise sucked down the water.
sentences.zh: 另一边是闪光的卡律布迪斯，伴随着可怕的咕噜声，吞下海水。

sentences.en: When she spewed it out, she seethed, all churning like a boiling cauldron.
sentences.zh: 当她把它喷出来时，她剧烈翻滚，就像一口沸腾的大锅。

sentences.en: On a huge fire, the froth flew high to spatter the topmost rocks on either side.
sentences.zh: 在熊熊烈火上，泡沫飞溅到两侧最高的岩石上。

sentences.en: But when she swallowed back the sea, she seemed all stirred from inside, and the rock around was roaring dreadfully, and the dark blue sand below was visible.
sentences.zh: 但当她把海水重新吞下时，她似乎从内部被完全搅动，周围的岩石发出可怕的轰鸣，下面深蓝色的沙子清晰可见。

sentences.en: The men were seized by fear.
sentences.zh: 男人们陷入了恐惧。

sentences.en: That is amazing.
sentences.zh: 那太惊人了。

sentences.en: I truly felt it in my heart.
sentences.zh: 我确实在内心深处感受到了。

sentences.en: Madeline, I assume you did too, listening to that.
sentences.zh: 玛德琳，我想你在听的时候也是如此。

sentences.en: I'm wondering what you thought when you first read this translation by Emily.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道你第一次读艾米莉的这个译本时作何感想。

sentences.en: Did it feel different to you?
sentences.zh: 对你来说感觉有什么不同吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, I loved it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: The moment that I really knew what an extraordinary piece of text this was is Charybdis and Scylla, and I remember being like, is he going to make it?
sentences.zh: 我真正知道这是一段非凡文本的时刻是卡律布迪斯和斯库拉，我记得当时想的是，他能成功吗？

sentences.en: And, you know, here's, like, I've spent years, decades of my life studying this poem.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我花了好几年，几十年的人生来研究这首诗。

sentences.en: I know he makes it.
sentences.zh: 我知道他成功了。

sentences.en: But, you know, I was so in the scene because of what Emily Wilson had done with the text
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，因为艾米莉·威尔逊对文本的处理

sentences.en: and with the excitement of the story that I, you know, I felt like I saw it again with new eyes.
sentences.zh: 以及故事的精彩，我完全沉浸在场景中，以至于我觉得自己仿佛用崭新的双眼重新看到了它。

sentences.en: So that is such a gift, and I love that.
sentences.zh: 所以这真是一份厚礼，我太喜欢了。

sentences.en: I feel the same way.
sentences.zh: 我有同感。

sentences.en: Madeline, let's talk about your work.
sentences.zh: 玛德琳，我们来谈谈你的作品。

sentences.en: You are a classics teacher turned noveliSt.
sentences.zh: 你曾是一名古典学老师，后来成为了小说家。

sentences.en: You've written a number of brilliant books and short stories.
sentences.zh: 你写了许多精彩的书籍和短篇小说。

sentences.en: Including Cersei, my personal favorite, which is about one of the goddesses that Odysseus encounters on his way home.
sentences.zh: 包括我个人最喜欢的《喀耳刻》，它讲述了奥德修斯在回家的路上遇到的女神之一。

sentences.en: She is the goddess of sorcery, and again, quick recap here, forgive me.
sentences.zh: 她是巫术女神，再次简单回顾一下，请原谅我。

sentences.en: Basically, she turns all of his men into pigs.
sentences.zh: 基本上，她把他的所有手下都变成猪。

sentences.en: He spends a year with her as her lover.
sentences.zh: 他作为她的情人与她共度了一年。

sentences.en: And eventually, everything gets resolved, and Odysseus moves on.
sentences.zh: 最终，一切都得到解决，奥德修斯继续前行。

sentences.en: Overall, Cersei is a relatively minor character in the Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，喀耳刻在《奥德赛》中是一个相对次要的角色。

sentences.en: But clearly, she's someone that you felt strongly enough about to base an entire book on.
sentences.zh: 但显然，你对她感受颇深，甚至以她为基础创作了一整本书。

sentences.en: Why is that?
sentences.zh: 这是为什么呢？

sentences.en: Like, what was it about her that you were so drawn to?
sentences.zh: 比如，她身上有什么吸引你的地方？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So one of the things that is so interesting is sort of the later versions of Cersei have really tended in a very negative direction.
sentences.zh: 所以其中一个非常有趣的事情是，关于喀耳刻的后世版本往往朝着非常消极的方向发展。

sentences.en: They've seen her as sort of the man-hater and the femme fatale and, you know, the spider at the center of her web.
sentences.zh: 人们把她视为厌男者、蛇蝎美人，你知道的，网中央的蜘蛛。

sentences.en: But in the Odyssey, if you actually go back to the Odyssey, yes, she does turn Odysseus' men into pigs.
sentences.zh: 但如果你真的回到《奥德赛》中，没错，她确实把奥德修斯的手下变成了猪。

sentences.en: But she also, after she and Odysseus come to an understanding, invites them to stay on her island as long as they need to stay.
sentences.zh: 但她也在她和奥德修斯达成共识后，邀请他们在她的岛上住多久都可以。

sentences.en: She, you know, helps them recover from the trauma that they've been going through.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，她帮助他们从经历过的创伤中恢复过来。

sentences.en: She offers them a place of peace and a haven.
sentences.zh: 她为他们提供了一个平静的避风港。

sentences.en: And then when they do decide to go, she doesn't hold them at all.
sentences.zh: 然后当他们决定离开时，她一点也没有挽留。

sentences.en: She says, fine.
sentences.zh: 她说，好吧。

sentences.en: And she gives them incredibly valuable advice for the journey ahead.
sentences.zh: 并且她为他们接下来的旅程提供了极其宝贵的建议。

sentences.en: So in the epic story, she represents an obstacle that he has to kind of tame or overcome.
sentences.zh: 所以在史诗故事中，她代表了他必须驯服或克服的障碍。

sentences.en: And then she offers him her help.
sentences.zh: 然后她向他提供帮助。

sentences.en: It kind of unlocks her help for him, which then she offers freely.
sentences.zh: 这实际上开启了她对他的帮助，随后她慷慨提供。

sentences.en: But we get nothing about, like, why is she turning men into pigs?
sentences.zh: 但我们完全不知道，她为什么要将男人们变成猪？

sentences.en: Odysseus, the most curious man in ancient literature, doesn't ask her.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯，古代文学中最具好奇心的人，并没有问她。

sentences.en: And so part of what really drew me to that is that all we get is Odysseus' version.
sentences.zh: 所以真正吸引我的一部分原因在于，我们得到的只有奥德修斯的版本。

sentences.en: It's literally him telling the story to some other people to make himself look good.
sentences.zh: 这纯粹是他在向其他人讲述这个故事，好让自己看起来很了不起。

sentences.en: And so I really wanted to know, who is Cersei?
sentences.zh: 所以我真的很想知道，喀耳刻是谁？

sentences.en: Why is she doing these things?
sentences.zh: 她为什么要这样做？

sentences.en: How did she come to have this witchy power?
sentences.zh: 她是如何拥有这种巫术力量的？

sentences.en: You know, I wanted to understand from her perspective, not from his perspective, why all that was happening.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我想从她的视角而不是他的视角去理解这一切为什么会发生。

sentences.en: Okay, this is making me think of a question that is actually for both of you.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这让我想到了一个实际上针对你们两个人的问题。

sentences.en: But Emily, I want to ask you firSt.
sentences.zh: 但艾米莉，我想先问你。

sentences.en: What were the things that were in the DNA of the story that you felt you absolutely had to maintain?
sentences.zh: 你觉得故事基因中有哪些东西是你认为绝对必须保持的？

sentences.en: These are kind of immovable parts.
sentences.zh: 这些算是不可动摇的部分。

sentences.en: And what were the things that you found to be movable or interpretable?
sentences.zh: 而你又发现哪些东西是可以变通或解释的？

sentences.en: How did you go about thinking about that, those questions?
sentences.zh: 你是如何思考这些问题的？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a really difficult question, I think, for any translation project is just because it's never going to be possible to replicate in totally different words for a totally
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为对任何翻译项目来说，这都是一个非常困难的问题，仅仅因为不可能在一种完全不同的文化中，用完全不同的词汇

sentences.en: different culture, every single element, every single syllable, every single sound of the original text.
sentences.zh: 去复制原文的每一个元素、每一个音节、每一个声音。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, I felt that, as I already said, the meter of the poem seemed essential to me.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，正如我刚才所说，我觉得这首诗的格律对我来说至关重要。

sentences.en: And also the multivocality seemed essential to me.
sentences.zh: 而且多重声音对我来说也至关重要。

sentences.en: Then there were other things where I thought I can convey some quality of this without being
sentences.zh: 然后还有其他一些事情，我认为我可以在并非

sentences.en: 100% one for one about it.
sentences.zh: 百分之百对应的情况下传达出某种特质。

sentences.en: And that included things like the fact that the original poem, because it's based on a centuries-long or pre-existing oral tradition, has a huge amount of repetition.
sentences.zh: 这包括这样一件事：由于最初的诗歌基于延续数个世纪或既有的口头传统，它包含大量的重复。

sentences.en: And so I thought I need to include some repetition.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我需要包含一些重复。

sentences.en: Everyone needs to have the iconic wine dark sea, wine dark sea, wine dark sea, some more wine dark sea.
sentences.zh: 每个人都需要听到标志性的酒红色的海，酒红色的海，酒红色的海，还有更多酒红色的海。

sentences.en: We need to have bright-eyed Athena, keep on being bright-eyed.
sentences.zh: 我们需要明眸的雅典娜，一直保持明眸。

sentences.en: We need to have Nestor being a horse lord over and over.
sentences.zh: 我们需要内斯特一遍又一遍地做着马王。

sentences.en: But it may be possible that you can get the idea that this is a repetitive formulaic text without it being absolutely 100% of the time when there's a repetition in the original,
sentences.zh: 但也许有可能，你可以让人体会到这是一部重复的公式化文本，而不需要在原文有重复的地方

sentences.en: does there need to be a repetition every single time in the translation?
sentences.zh: 每一次翻译时都绝对百分之百地进行重复？

sentences.en: Maybe I can convey that quality actually more vividly by repeating some amount of times, but maybe not 100% of the amount of times.
sentences.zh: 也许我可以通过重复一定次数，而不是百分之百地重复，来更生动地传达这种特质。

sentences.en: How did you choose what to vary?
sentences.zh: 你是如何选择哪些地方要变化的？

sentences.en: Obviously, part of the reason why there was so much repetition, one of you told me this at some point in all of the things you've written or said, part of the reason was that
sentences.zh: 显然，有那么多重复的部分，原因之一——你们中的某个人在你的所有著作或言论中的某个时刻告诉我过——部分原因在于

sentences.en: Bards, it helped them remember the story, right?
sentences.zh: 吟游诗人，这帮助他们记住故事，对吧？

sentences.en: It was like a device where they could just kind of remember that Athena has bright eyes,
sentences.zh: 这就像一种装置，能让他们记住雅典娜有明亮的眼睛，

sentences.en: Athena has bright eyes.
sentences.zh: 雅典娜有明亮的眼睛。

sentences.en: How did you make the decision about what to sub in if there was a new way of describing her or one of these other characters?
sentences.zh: 当有了一种描述她或这些其他角色的新方法时，你是如何决定替换什么的？

sentences.en: I mean, so I thought in some ways, if I'm going to vary sometimes, then that's an opportunity
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在某些方面我认为，如果我有选择地进行变化，那么这就是一个机会，

sentences.en: to lean into the fact that some of these epithets, which is the standard formulaic describing words
sentences.zh: 去顺应这样一个事实：其中一些贬义词（即用于这些角色或诗中名词的标准公式化描述词），

sentences.en: for these characters or the nouns in the poem, some of these have multiple different meanings.
sentences.zh: 其中一些具有多种不同的含义。

sentences.en: So if possible, I want to be able to convey, for instance, that when Odysseus is described, as he repeatedly is, as polu class, which means much enduring or resilient, or he's gone
sentences.zh: 因此，如果可能的话，我希望能够传达出，例如，当奥德修斯被反复描述为polu class时，这意味着极其坚韧或百折不挠，或者他经历了

sentences.en: through a lot, or this guy is capable of going through a lot, he's got grit, he's stubborn.
sentences.zh: 很多，或者这家伙有能力经历很多，他很有毅力，他很固执。

sentences.en: If I can change how I translate that to fit a different context, then I'm going to give
sentences.zh: 如果我能改变我翻译它的方式以适应不同的语境，那么我将

sentences.en: the reader or the listener more of the all-around characterization of the character, because the original word connotes all of those things.
sentences.zh: 给读者或听众提供关于这个角色的更多全方位性格刻画，因为原词暗示了所有这些事情。

sentences.en: And so I can lean into maybe in this scene where Odysseus is weeping as he remembers the Trojan war, maybe then he's polu class, as in he's a veteran of wars.
sentences.zh: 因此，也许在这个奥德修斯因想起特洛伊战争而哭泣的场景中，他是polu class，也就是战争老兵。

sentences.en: But maybe he's stubborn if he's polu class when he's plotting the murder of his wife's suitors.
sentences.zh: 但如果他在密谋谋杀妻子的求婚者时是polu class，那他可能就是固执的。

sentences.en: So there might be ways I can shape the epithets to fit the context of a particular scene.
sentences.zh: 所以也许有办法我可以塑造这些称号来适应特定场景的语境。

sentences.en: Madeline, how did you think about this question, about what you wanted to be loyal to and what you would diverge from?
sentences.zh: 玛德琳，你是如何思考这个问题的，关于你想要忠于什么以及你会偏离什么？

sentences.en: In other words, what was the guiding principle there as you thought about how off-script you might go?
sentences.zh: 换句话说，当你在考虑自己可能会走多偏离剧本时，指导原则是什么？

sentences.en: The guiding principle for me was Circe's agency and the fact that this was her story and the idea
sentences.zh: 对我的指导原则是喀耳刻的自主性，以及这是一个关于她的故事这一事实，还有这样一个想法：

sentences.en: that the story of a woman's life and growth into sort of her vocation and her role as an artist which is how witchcraft functions for me is enough.
sentences.zh: 一个女人的一生及其成长为某种职业以及她作为艺术家的角色（对我而言巫术就是这样运作的）的故事，这就足够了。

sentences.en: That is story.
sentences.zh: 这就是故事。

sentences.en: When you are adapting, there really are no rules.
sentences.zh: 当你进行改编时，真的没有什么规则。

sentences.en: You can write very close to the text and not be successful and very far from the text and be completely successful.
sentences.zh: 你可以紧贴文本写却并不成功，也可以远离文本写却完全成功。

sentences.en: I feel like what makes for a successful retelling is how true and sort of fully fleshed the vision that the writer has is.
sentences.zh: 我觉得一个成功的复述的关键在于，作者的愿景是多么真实和丰满。

sentences.en: I love writing close to the text personally, but I also like overturning it and arguing with it.
sentences.zh: 我个人喜欢紧贴文本写作，但我也喜欢颠覆它并与之争论。

sentences.en: And so I love sort of pushing back on, okay, that was Odysseus's version of the story that he's been able to dine out on for, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢回击，好吧，那是奥德修斯的故事版本，他靠它招摇撞骗了，你知道的，

sentences.en: 3,000 years.
sentences.zh: 三千年。

sentences.en: Let's have someone else's perspective on these scenes.
sentences.zh: 让我们换成别人的视角来看这些场景。

sentences.en: So there were moments where I really enjoyed contradicting, but there were also so many moments where I loved going right into the
sentences.zh: 所以有些时刻我真的很享受反其道而行之，但也有很多时刻我喜欢直接深入到

sentences.en: text and picking something up and, you know, transforming it or allowing it to really inform
sentences.zh: 文本中，挑选出一些东西，然后，你知道的，转化它或者让它真正融入

sentences.en: Cersei.
sentences.zh: 喀耳刻。

sentences.en: One of the most important descriptions of her that really informed the whole novel was the description of her as speaking like a human.
sentences.zh: 对她最重要、真正支撑整部小说的描述之一，就是将她描述为像人类一样说话。

sentences.en: And I was like, what does it mean to be a god who speaks like a human?
sentences.zh: 当时我在想，作为一个像人类一样说话的神意味着什么？

sentences.en: And so, you know, then as a novelist, my imagination and my invention could work upon that incredibly rich term that Homer gave me.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，作为一个小说家，我的想象力和创造力就可以在这个荷美尔给我的极其丰富的词汇上发挥作用。

sentences.en: What did it mean for you to speak like a human?
sentences.zh: 像人类一样说话对你来说意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, for me, I started thinking about first what it meant to speak like a god, which is that in the ancient stories, when gods speak to humans, oftentimes humans will fall to
sentences.zh: 嗯，对我来说，我开始思考首先像神一样说话意味着什么，也就是说在古代故事中，当神对人类说话时，人类往往会双膝下跪

sentences.en: their knees and their blood runs cold and their hair stands on end.
sentences.zh: 血液凝固，毛骨悚然。

sentences.en: There's like this very physical response to being in the presence of a god who is, you know, commanding your attention and showing you their power.
sentences.zh: 身处一个正在，你知道的，发号施令并向你展示力量的神面前，会有一种非常生理性的反应。

sentences.en: And so if you are speaking like a mortal, it means you sound weak compared to them.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你像凡人一样说话，就意味着听起来比他们虚弱。

sentences.en: And so that immediately, in my imagination, put Cersei kind of at the bottom of the hierarchy.
sentences.zh: 所以在我的想象中，这立刻把喀耳刻放在了金字塔的底层。

sentences.en: And it made her, in a sense, an outcast to, you know, these incredibly powerful gods that she's surrounded by.
sentences.zh: 在某种意义上，这使她成为了那些围绕着她的极其强大的神明们的局外人。

sentences.en: That's so fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太迷人了。

sentences.en: And it makes me think of the reaction that all this interpretation of the text gets.
sentences.zh: 这让我想到了对文本所有这种诠释所引发的反应。

sentences.en: And I guess I wonder, Emily, your translation got this huge response, including some criticism from some Odyssey obsessives.
sentences.zh: 我想知道，艾米莉，你的译本获得了巨大的反响，包括来自一些《奥德赛》狂热爱好者的批评。

sentences.en: On your website, you have these three buttons.
sentences.zh: 在你的网站上，你有这三个按钮。

sentences.en: One is for media requests, another is for general inquiries, and a third is for misogynistic trolling.
sentences.zh: 一个是用于媒体请求，另一个用于一般咨询，第三个用于厌女症网民的恶意骚扰。

sentences.en: So it does seem as though you're getting quite a fair bit of that.
sentences.zh: 所以看起来你确实遭到了相当多的攻击。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I got a bit of that.
sentences.zh: 我确实遇到了一些。

sentences.en: I wonder how you engage with people who, in good faith, say and feel that you strayed too far from the words and the meaning of the text in Homer.
sentences.zh: 我很想知道你是如何与那些出于善意、认为并感觉你偏离荷美尔文本的词语和含义太远的人互动的。

sentences.en: I mean, honestly, I would dispute the idea that the misogynistic trolls or the trolls of various kinds are actually obsessed with the Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 说实话，我会反驳这样一种观点，即厌女网民或各种网民真的对《奥德赛》痴迷。

sentences.en: I mean, I'd love to have an actual conversation with any one of them about what do you make of line 52 in book 13.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我很乐意与他们中的任何一个人进行真正的对话，探讨你对第13卷第52行作何感想。

sentences.en: I mean, I'm really interested in the interpretation of that Greek phrase.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我真的对那个希腊短语的解释很感兴趣。

sentences.en: We would all love to watch that, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我们都很想看那个。

sentences.en: That's never what happens, right?
sentences.zh: 但那从来不会发生，对吧？

sentences.en: It's all just online performativity about modern notions about masculinity and greatness and actually whiteness and Westernness as well.
sentences.zh: 这一切都只是关于现代关于男子气概、伟大以及实际上还有白人性和西方性的在线表演主义。

sentences.en: None of that is about the Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 这些都与《奥德赛》无关。

sentences.en: The Odyssey is this really complex portrayal of a heros, which in the archaic context,
sentences.zh: 《奥德赛》是对一个英雄的非常复杂的刻画，在古代语境中，

sentences.en: means this outsized character who performs outsized deeds and he wins kleos, he wins eternal glory through this ability to do extraordinary things which no other mortal could do.
sentences.zh: 这意味着一个庞大的人物，他做出了庞大的壮举，他通过这种完成其他凡人无法完成的非凡事迹的能力赢得了克莱奥斯，赢得了永恒的荣耀。

sentences.en: He has a homecoming journey which is impossibly long and he spends eight years with two different goddesses.
sentences.zh: 他的归家之旅长得不可思议，他与两位不同的女神共度了八年。

sentences.en: Most mortals don't get to do that.
sentences.zh: 大多数凡人没有机会做到这一点。

sentences.en: Most mortals don't fight in a war that lasts 10 years and devise a wooden horse and manage to outwit everybody and slaughter huge numbers of people despite being completely out
sentences.zh: 大多数凡人不会参加长达10年的战争，发明木马，设法智胜所有人，并在自己家中遭到完全压制的情况下，

sentences.en: outmatched in his own house.
sentences.zh: 屠杀大量的人。

sentences.en: So he's both a warrior hero and a trickster hero and a strategy hero.
sentences.zh: 所以他既是战士英雄，又是诡计英雄和策略英雄。

sentences.en: Within the archaic context, is there the kind of judgment about, oh, we don't like dishonesty that there is in later cultures?
sentences.zh: 在古代语境中，是否存在那种认为“哦，我们不喜欢不诚实”的评判，就像后世文化中那样？

sentences.en: I don't think there is.
sentences.zh: 我认为并没有。

sentences.en: I think there's much more open-mindedness about, yes, one of his skills is he can tell any story and he can talk out of many different sides of his mouth.
sentences.zh: 我认为人们对“是的，他的技能之一是他能讲任何故事，他能从许多不同的立场说话”持有更开放的态度。

sentences.en: He's really good at that.
sentences.zh: 他真的很擅长这个。

sentences.en: That's an important skill.
sentences.zh: 这是一项重要的技能。

sentences.en: Okay, if we set aside the not obsessives, what about the people, like, what do you say to the
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果我们抛开那些不痴迷的人，那么对于那些人，比如，你对那些确实阅读文本、确实关心它并对你选择的词语或处理文本的方式提出异议的人说些什么？

sentences.en: people who do read the text, who do care about it and take issue with some of the words you chose or the way you went about the text?
sentences.zh: 比如，你认为这种过分珍视、对人们视为关于这东西的所谓“正确”翻译版本的保护欲，是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: Like, where do you think it comes from, that feeling of
sentences.zh: 我觉得这挺奇怪的。

sentences.en: preciousness, of protectiveness over what people view to be the, quote, unquote, correct version of a translation of this thing?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，即使是对那些不那么恶意的网民，我认为认为一本书或一种翻译会抹杀其他翻译的想法也挺奇怪的。

sentences.en: I think it's quite odd.
sentences.zh: 这挺奇怪的。

sentences.en: I mean, even with the less trolley kind of people, I think it's quite odd to think that one book or one translation erases the others.
sentences.zh: 这挺奇怪的。

sentences.en: I mean, if people prefer some other translation or if people want to read the Greek, I would love for them to do that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果人们更喜欢别的翻译，或者人们想去读希腊语原文，我都非常乐意看到他们这么做。

sentences.en: I think it's great.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这很好。

sentences.en: I have no desire to legislate about which versions of the Odyssey or of any ancient text people want to engage with.
sentences.zh: 我根本不想去规定人们究竟该去阅读哪个版本的《奥德赛》或是哪部古代文本。

sentences.en: So I think there's something quite strange about the idea that the canon doesn't have room for many, many different interpretations, translations, engagements, reinventions.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得，那种认为经典容不下形形色色、许许多多不同的解读、翻译、重塑和再创作的想法，是一件相当奇怪的事情。

sentences.en: In a way, it's like, you know, wanting there to be only one production of King Lear ever.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上讲，这就好比，你知道的，希望世上永远只存在过一版《李尔王》的演出一样。

sentences.en: And that's it.
sentences.zh: 然后就再也没有了。

sentences.en: It's absurd.
sentences.zh: 这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: No other productions.
sentences.zh: 没有其他的制作。

sentences.en: No other ideas.
sentences.zh: 没有其他的创意。

sentences.en: You know, of course, you want as many productions and fabulous productions out there as possible.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当然，你会希望有尽可能多的制作以及精彩绝伦的制作呈现于世。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it just, I always find it very confusing when people get so agitated.
sentences.zh: 所以每次看到人们反应如此激进，我都觉得非常困惑。

sentences.en: And I think what, maybe what they're really saying is, I had an important experience emotionally with one version of this text, and that's great.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得他们真正在表达的可能其实是：我在这个文本的某一版本中获得了深刻的情感体验，这很好。

sentences.en: Which is sweet.
sentences.zh: 这很温馨。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: So you don't need to get angry about it.
sentences.zh: 所以你没必要为此感到生气。

sentences.en: That's fine.
sentences.zh: 这没关系。

sentences.en: I'm happy for you that you had that.
sentences.zh: 我为你曾有过这样的体验感到高兴。

sentences.en: So from the outside, I think something that joins your work for me is that both of you share this idea that this ancient text needed to matter to people, not necessarily in like
sentences.zh: 所以从外人的角度来看，我觉得两位的作品中有一个共同点，那就是你们都认同这个观点：这部古代文本需要与人们产生紧密的联结，而不一定是以那种

sentences.en: a highfalutin academic way.
sentences.zh: 高高在上的学术方式。

sentences.en: It needed to matter to people viscerally.
sentences.zh: 它需要深入人们的内心，产生刻骨铭心的触动。

sentences.en: And you both dedicated years of your life making that happen, making this story more popularly understood.
sentences.zh: 你们俩都为此奉献了多年的生命，让这一切成为现实，让这个故事能够被大众所理解。

sentences.en: So my question is why?
sentences.zh: 所以我的问题是，为什么？

sentences.en: Like, what have you each come to understand about the transcendence of the
sentences.zh: 比方说，你们各自对《奥德赛》的超凡魅力、

sentences.en: Odyssey, about its universality?
sentences.zh: 对其普世价值有了怎样的理解？

sentences.en: I mean, I hesitate about universality because, of course, the Odyssey has meant different things in different moments of history, right, to different people.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我对“普世价值”这个词有所保留，因为当然了，《奥德赛》在历史的不同时期、对于不同的人而言，一直都有着不同的意义，对吧？

sentences.en: But I think the other section of your your question, I absolutely, I think the original poem for me, but I'm also so much not alone in this, is deeply moving.
sentences.zh: 但我觉得你问题的另一部分，我绝对赞同，我认为对我而言——而且有这种感受的人绝不仅我一个——这部最初的史诗深深地打动了我。

sentences.en: It's, there's so many big emotions in Homer.
sentences.zh: 荷马的作品中蕴含着太多强烈的情感。

sentences.en: There are so many characters feeling enormous amounts of both rage and grief and joy and excitement.
sentences.zh: 里面有那么多角色，体验着极其剧烈的愤怒、悲伤、喜悦和兴奋。

sentences.en: And those qualities seem to me not always legible in all translations that I've looked at or read.
sentences.zh: 在我看过或读过的所有翻译中，这些特质似乎并非总是能在每部译作中都清晰可见。

sentences.en: So I want to convey that in English however I can.
sentences.zh: 所以我无论如何都想在英语中把这一点传达出来。

sentences.en: And Madeline?
sentences.zh: 玛德琳呢？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I think it's incredibly exciting to read.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得读起来真的非常激动人心。

sentences.en: And I always find it a magical moment when I read an ancient text and I see a piece of myself that just, you know, speaks right through the millennia, right to me and my situation.
sentences.zh: 每当我阅读古代文本，看到其中展现的某个部分的自己，那种跨越数千年、直接对我以及我所处境况诉说的感觉，我总是觉得这是一种神奇的时刻。

sentences.en: Even if I'm, you know, not understanding it 100% the way an ancient audience would have understood it, still feeling that resonance of things that humans have struggled
sentences.zh: 即便我，你知道的，并不百分之百像古代受众那样去理解它，但依然能感受到那种共鸣：人类自古以来就在与之抗争的种种事物，你知道的，

sentences.en: with from time immemorial, you know, and knowing that the grief I might carry is resonating down through the centuries with all the other people who have resonated with that.
sentences.zh: 并且知道我所承载的悲伤，正在历经岁月的长河，与所有产生过共鸣的人们遥相呼应。

sentences.en: That's a really magical and powerful thing.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一件既神奇又充满力量的事情。

sentences.en: And then at the same time to get lost in the things that are very different.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，又能沉浸在那些截然不同的事物之中。

sentences.en: It's such an endlessly interesting and I would say generous world that Homer has created,
sentences.zh: 荷马所创造的世界是一个如此充满无限趣味、而且我要说非常宽广包容的世界，

sentences.en: that any one of these characters, not just Odysseus who stands at the center, but any one of these characters could be their own novel.
sentences.zh: 以至于这些角色中的任何一个——不仅仅是处于核心地位的奥德修斯，而是其中的任何一个人——都能撑起一部属于他们自己的小说。

sentences.en: They could be their own epic.
sentences.zh: 他们都可以拥有属于自己的史诗。

sentences.en: You know, all of these characters are interesting and valuable and the world feels so big and inviting and open.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，所有这些角色都既有趣又有价值，这个世界感觉如此宏大、迷人而又开放。

sentences.en: And it's just such a pleasure to spend time in it.
sentences.zh: 置身其中简直是一种无上的享受。

sentences.en: And so I love to sort of help facilitate other people to have that experience because I love it so much.
sentences.zh: 所以我非常乐意去协助他人获得这种体验，因为我自己太爱它了。

sentences.en: Okay, we're going to take a quick break.
sentences.zh: 好了，我们要进行短暂的休息。

sentences.en: And when we come back, we are going to spend time talking about all of those characters that made us all fall in love with this book.
sentences.zh: 等我们回来后，将花时间探讨所有那些让我们爱上这本书的角色。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 甚至早在黑胶唱片时代我在夜店当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带着300张你最珍爱的宝贝去上班。

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你把一个DJ台变成了一个充满活力的快闪博物馆，里面摆满了美丽动人的50年历史的老物件。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜爱的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times Games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《纽约时报》游戏旗下的拼字游戏《联线》。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢试图套路你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Azersky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·阿泽斯基，我每天负责创作《拼字蜜蜂》和《字母连线》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做联觉的奇特现象。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到声音的这些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com slash games，今天就开始游玩吧。

sentences.en: To the point about the eternal resonance of these characters and how they reach through the millennia, we want to do a who's who of the Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 说到这些角色的永恒共鸣以及他们如何跨越千年，我们想对《奥德赛》里的人物做一个盘点。

sentences.en: And we're going to focus on the main characters, the ones that appear in the movie.
sentences.zh: 我们将重点关注主要角色，也就是电影中出现的那几位。

sentences.en: Let's start with our hero, Odysseus.
sentences.zh: 让我们从我们的英雄奥德修斯开始。

sentences.en: Emily, your translation of the Odyssey famously starts with a line that Christopher Nolan himself has cited as part of his inspiration for making this movie.
sentences.zh: 艾米莉，你的《奥德赛》译本以一句名言闻名，克里斯托弗·诺兰本人曾引用这句话，作为他拍摄这部电影的灵感来源之一。

sentences.en: Christopher Nolan is famously drawn to obsessive, flawed protagonists, so I think it's apt.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，克里斯托弗·诺兰对那种充满执念、有缺陷的主角情有独钟，所以我认为这很贴切。

sentences.en: And that starting line is, tell me about a complicated man.
sentences.zh: 而那句开场白是：告诉我，那个饱经风霜的复杂男人。

sentences.en: So why is Odysseus complicated?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么奥德修斯很复杂呢？

sentences.en: He's complicated because he's multiple in ways that no other Homeric hero is.
sentences.zh: 他之所以复杂，是因为他具有其他荷马史诗英雄所没有的多面性。

sentences.en: Odysseus is always going to take the roundabout way.
sentences.zh: 奥德修斯总是会选择走弯路。

sentences.en: He's going to be constantly disguising himself as someone else.
sentences.zh: 他会不断地把自己伪装成别人。

sentences.en: One of his great skills is code switching.
sentences.zh: 他最伟大的技能之一就是语码转换。

sentences.en: He can survive those multiple years of being lost, being in multiple different environments, facing threats that no other Homeric hero manages to
sentences.zh: 他能够在那长达数年的迷失中存活下来，身处各种不同的环境，面对其他任何荷马英雄都无法应对的威胁、

sentences.en: survive, surviving goddesses and man-eating giants, surviving all of the threats that face him once he's
sentences.zh: 在女神和吃人巨人的手下生还，在他回到自己的家乡岛屿伊塔卡之后，还要在面对那些围攻他家或者已经闯入他家的男人们时化险为夷。

sentences.en: back on his home island of Ithaca, of the men who are besieging his house or who are already inside his house.
sentences.zh: （译文对应上一句后半部分省略的补全，但在此处按原句顺序完整呈现）

sentences.en: He has this capacity for self-reinvention and for having multiple identities, which is very different from anyone else in the universe, in the Homeric universe.
sentences.zh: 他具备这种自我重塑以及拥有多重身份的能力，这与荷马宇宙中的任何其他人都有着极大的不同。

sentences.en: Madeline, what about the complexity of his duality?
sentences.zh: 玛德琳，他这种二元性的复杂性体现在哪里？

sentences.en: You know, he's the smartest guy in the room, but he's also the most ruthless.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他是屋里最聪明的人，但同时也是最冷酷无情的。

sentences.en: He's murderous and he's also devoted to his family.
sentences.zh: 他既会杀戮，又对家庭无比忠诚。

sentences.en: He spends this whole book trying to get home to them.
sentences.zh: 他花了一整本书的时间试图回到家人身边。

sentences.en: How do you think about those things?
sentences.zh: 你是如何看待这些特质的？

sentences.en: Well, the piece that really resonated with me is the psychological aspect of, you know, kind of
sentences.zh: 嗯，真正与我产生共鸣的是心理层面，你知道的，有点像

sentences.en: looking at what it means to have survived what he survived and how that would shape him.
sentences.zh: 去审视经历过他所经历的一切意味着什么，以及那会如何塑造他。

sentences.en: And of course, his journey is not glorious and his house is not glorious unless it's full of people who haven't chosen to be there.
sentences.zh: 当然，如果他的归乡之旅不是充满了那些并非自愿留在那里的普通人，那他的旅程就毫无荣耀可言，他的家也算不上荣耀。

sentences.en: And Madeline, what about your beloved Cersei?
sentences.zh: 玛德琳，你挚爱的瑟茜呢？

sentences.en: Are you going to be watching those scenes with great apprehension?
sentences.zh: 你看那些场景时会感到无比忧虑吗？

sentences.en: No, I mean, anytime I'm watching an adaptation of The Odyssey, I want more of the women.
sentences.zh: 不，我的意思是，无论什么时候看《奥德赛》的改编，我都希望看到更多关于女性的内容。

sentences.en: Calypso gets to have her monologue and, you know, she kind of gets to put a little bit more of her perspective out there.
sentences.zh: 卡吕普索有机会发表她的独白，你知道的，她算是有机会更多地表达她自己的视角。

sentences.en: But so many of the women are just kept as these sort of mysterious figures who come in and help or obstruct.
sentences.zh: 但太多的女性只是被当成那种神秘的人物，她们登场，提供帮助或是制造阻碍。

sentences.en: And that's just how they function in The Odyssey.
sentences.zh: 而她们在《奥德赛》中就是这样发挥作用的。

sentences.en: So
sentences.zh: 所以

sentences.en: I'm just going to be yearning for more of their stories, as I always do.
sentences.zh: 我只会像往常一样，渴望听到更多关于她们的故事。

sentences.en: You know that.
sentences.zh: 你知道的。

sentences.en: You already know it.
sentences.zh: 你早就知道了。

sentences.en: I'm at peace.
sentences.zh: 我已经释怀了。

sentences.en: I'm at peace.
sentences.zh: 我已经释怀了。

sentences.en: You're resigned to it.
sentences.zh: 你已经认命了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: I want to end by asking what you're hoping that people take away from experiencing this movie.
sentences.zh: 最后我想问，你希望大家从观看这部电影中获得什么感悟？

sentences.en: Like, is there a moment or a line or a lesson in it that you think applies uniquely to the world that we're living in now?
sentences.zh: 比如，其中是否有某个时刻、某句台词或某条教训，你认为它独特地适用于我们现今生活的世界？

sentences.en: And that if you could do it yourself, you would leave people with if this was your movie?
sentences.zh: 如果由你亲自操刀，如果是你的电影，你会给观众留下什么？

sentences.en: I mean, I think one of the big themes of The Odyssey that very much resonates with our time is the importance of welcoming the stranger into your house, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我认为《奥德赛》的一大主题与我们的时代高度共鸣，那就是欢迎陌生人来到你家中的重要性，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, the whole poem is about hospitality and about the fact that the suitors of Odysseus have abused his hospitality by going
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，整首诗都是关于热情好客的，讲的是奥德修斯的求婚者们滥用了他的好客之道，未经邀请就闯入

sentences.en: into his house and hitting on his wife without being invited to do so.
sentences.zh: 他的家中，还调戏他的妻子。

sentences.en: It's all about the violations of hospitality and then the dangers of what happens when hospitality is violated and when people don't
sentences.zh: 整部作品都在探讨对好客之道的破坏，以及当好客之道遭到破坏时会带来什么危险，当人们没有

sentences.en: recognize that the poor and strangers are blessed by Zeus.
sentences.zh: 意识到穷人和陌生人是受宙斯保佑的时又会发生什么。

sentences.en: I loved that part of your translation.
sentences.zh: 我太喜欢你翻译的那一部分了。

sentences.en: And I also got that, honestly, Madeline, from reading your work, just this idea that you have to be a good hoSt. I say this not just as a podcast host,
sentences.zh: 说实话，玛德琳，从阅读你的作品中我也体会到了这一点，也就是你必须做一个好主人的这种观念。我这么说不仅仅是以播客主持人的身份，

sentences.en: but as a human being, this idea that when somebody shows up at your door, you know, you should offer them what you have and listen to them.
sentences.zh: 而是作为一个普通人，这种观念即：当有人出现在你门口时，你知道的，你应该把力所能及的食物拿出来招待他们并倾听他们。

sentences.en: That just felt like a kind of wonderful thing to keep in mind always.
sentences.zh: 这感觉真是一件值得永远铭记的美好事情。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Because, and, you know, the other half of that is because you don't know when it's going to be you, you know, that we all need to do this.
sentences.zh: 因为，你知道的，这背后的另一半原因是，你永远不知道什么时候轮到你遭遇这一切，你知道的，我们所有人都需要这样做。

sentences.en: This is sort of this great exchange that we all have to take part in.
sentences.zh: 这可以说是我们所有人都必须参与其中的一场伟大的互惠交流。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: No one belongs everywhere, right?
sentences.zh: 没有人能在任何地方都如鱼得水，对吧？

sentences.en: And the poem really teaches you that.
sentences.zh: 这首诗确实教会了你这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, I want to thank you both for coming on the show.
sentences.zh: 好的，我要感谢两位的到来。

sentences.zh: 埃米莉和玛德琳，这真是一次极大的荣幸。

sentences.zh: 对我来说也非常愉快。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: It's always so lovely to talk to you, Madeline.
sentences.zh: 跟你聊天总是这么愉快，玛德琳。

sentences.en: Yes, it's always great to speak with you.
sentences.zh: 是的，跟你交谈总是棒极了。

sentences.en: And thank you so much for having us.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢邀请我们来做客。

sentences.zh: 你们是很棒的嘉宾。谢谢。
